summary: No held thesis was broken by news today. The book lost 0.53% (-$3.22) while the SPY benchmark fell about 3.6% (560.38 to 539.98). The VOO, VTI, FAST and EXEL sales filled at the open, and the book's only rising lines were WMT (+1.7%), TLT (+1.2%) and KR (+0.7%). The news input explains none of that move. It holds single-name fiscal.ai items only, with no macro, rates, index-ETF or crypto headline for a fourth straight session, so the PM and Market Analyst should read the day from prices and not expect a cause from me. The day's real single-name news reaction came on SAM. It fell 5.0% on the first session after the 11-19 after-close founder-CEO handover (8-K 5.02), against about -3.6% for SPY, so it lagged by about 1.4 points. That is a mild negative read of the succession, not a clause trip, and it now sits 3.3% above its $201 stop, the closest of any holding. Applying L2, I checked every holding's own earnings estimate and 7-day filings. No holding has a print inside 5 trading days, and no holding has an 8-K 4.01, 4.02, new 5.02 or large 1.01/2.01 beyond SAM's 5.02, which is already handled.
upcoming: Held names: SAM's new CEO (Phil Hodges) takes over 11-23. Watch for any follow-up 8-K 5.02 or 7.01 that states founder Jim Koch's continuing role, which the inputs still do not give. SAM's 11-13 8-K 8.01 leaves the 7-day window after today unread, so it closes by expiry. KR's company-confirmed Q3 call is 12-03. That is 8 trading days out (11-26 closed), so it enters the 5-day window on 11-25. The 11-19 CRFB baby-food report has had no follow-up: no recall, no agency action, no filing. The 10-17 grocery-chain cyber item in KR's clause is now over a month old with no confirmation, so it is close to having come to nothing. WMT's next earnings date is still unverified, because the file still shows 11-19. IDXX (2027-02-01), INCY (2027-02-09), CARG (2027-02-18), DPZ (2027-02-22), MSCI (2027-01-27), VRSN (2027-02-04) and SAM (2027-02-23) are file estimates with nothing in the window. INCY and VRSN insider sales (11-17, 11-18, 11-19) brought nothing new today. TLT (bought today at $80.75) rose 1.2% on a day SPY fell about 3.6%, which fits its 'duration hedging' premise for one day; that is not graded evidence. Its next dated event is the 12-09 FOMC, and the input has carried no rates item since 11-16. Its $76.30 stop is about 5.5% under the $80.75 fill, not 5% under the $80.35 reference close; the PM should restate it per L6. Sold today: FAST's Baird downgrade to Neutral (11-20, $56 PT) continues the Industrials-avoid case, but the $56 target sits about 6.7% above the $52.50 sale price, so the downgrade is a rating call, not a price-target warning. EXEL filled at $65.95, just above its $65 stop. Not held, inside or near the window: ADSK and BBY have estimated prints on 11-24 (last year's date + 364 days, approximate, with no confirming headline or 8-K), 2 trading days out. GLD's 11-24 'earnings' entry is a data artifact. BLBD's file still shows 11-23, but the company-confirmed date is 12-02 (headline 11-18), so ignore the file estimate. UNFI has an estimated 12-01 print, and its 11-17 8-K 7.01 is still unexplained. ADBE has an estimated 12-09 print, the same day as the FOMC. CVS escalated: CMS has now proposed a named rule (CMS-6098-P, Medicare Advantage audit recoveries reaching back to 2018), the first concrete agency action after the 11-18 reimbursement report and Warren's breakup call. That continues the negative drift since 11-10, though CVS is not held. LNG's 11-17 8-K 1.01/2.03 is still unexplained (financing inference unchanged; RBC raised its PT 11-19). FTDR's 11-12 8-K 5.02 and DBX's 11-12 8-K have left the window unread, so both close by expiry. AAPL's camera-software chief departure is a report, not an 8-K, and AAPL is not held. Crypto: no BTC or ETH item for a fourth day; nothing is held there.
